findings.title: QuantAgent: Price-Driven Multi-Agent LLMs for High-Frequency Trading
findings.summary: Four specialized LLM agents (Indicator, Pattern, Trend, Risk) collaborate to make high-frequency trading decisions directly from OHLC price data, achieving 80% directional accuracy in zero-shot evaluation.
findings.relevance_notes: Directly maps to George's trading research harness. Architecture (specialized agents per signal type) mirrors how George could decompose candlestick + macro + factor signals.

findings.title: mem-agent: Equipping LLM Agents with Memory Using RL
findings.summary: A 4B LLM trained with GSPO to use markdown files as persistent memory via Python tools, inspired by Obsidian; includes MCP server for any LLM to use as a memory backend.
findings.relevance_notes: George already uses MEMORY.md as primary state. This paper validates that architecture and adds RL-based memory management (retrieve, update, clarify). The mem-agent-mcp server could be integrated.

findings.title: From AI Assistant to AI Scientist: POISE — Autonomous Discovery of LLM-RL Algorithms
findings.summary: POISE is a closed-loop LLM agent framework that autonomously discovers improved RL policy optimization algorithms, using evolutionary search with genealogically linked reflections, improving AIME25 pass@32 from 26.7% to 43.3%.
findings.relevance_notes: Meta-level relevance: the dream cycle IS George's version of POISE — iterative self-improvement via reflection + structured evidence. Confirms the architecture is well-founded.

findings.title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
findings.summary: Proposes a Zettelkasten-style interconnected memory network where notes dynamically link to each other, enabling better retrieval and reasoning than flat storage.
findings.relevance_notes: George's MEMORY.md is flat. A-MEM suggests linking related facts (e.g. trading findings → product ideas → research agenda) for better recall and reasoning.

findings.title: SimpleMem: Efficient Lifelong Memory for LLM Agents
findings.summary: Semantic lossless compression for agent memory achieves 64% performance boost over Claude-Mem on LoCoMo benchmark.
findings.relevance_notes: Relevant when MEMORY.md grows beyond manageable size. Current state is still compact enough that compression isn't needed yet.

findings.title: CORAL: Dynamic Information-Flow Orchestrator for Multi-Agent Systems
findings.summary: Replaces predefined multi-agent workflows with a dynamic natural-language A2A communication orchestrator, improving flexibility in long-horizon tasks.
findings.relevance_notes: Relevant to George's swarm/team tasks. Less critical than memory and trading papers.

findings.title: AndroTMem: Anchored Memory for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
findings.summary: Persistent interaction-trajectory memory for GUI agents navigating long-horizon tasks without losing context.
findings.relevance_notes: Tangentially relevant to agent-browser skill. Low priority for George's core use cases.

findings.title: From Spark to Fire: Error Cascade Mitigation in Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
findings.summary: Models and mitigates error propagation across agent chains in multi-agent LLM systems.
findings.relevance_notes: Relevant to George's swarm tasks — errors in one sub-agent can cascade. Could inform how George validates teammate outputs.

findings.title: OpenClaw: Breakout AI Agent Framework
findings.summary: Fastest-growing open-source AI agent framework (210k+ stars), modular plugin-based LLM orchestration. Memory stored in markdown files — similar to NanoClaw/George architecture.
findings.relevance_notes: Architecture validation rather than actionable insight. George is already implemented and running.

findings.title: Memento-Skills: Let Agents Design Agents
findings.summary: Agents autonomously design and store reusable skill modules, enabling continual capability growth.
findings.relevance_notes: Dream cycle already mirrors this — George stages new scripts each night. Formalizing a skill library could be next evolution.
